correctness.rationale: The normalized-gain rule selects the minimum Gaussian tail/leading ratio exactly. The ratio law is half-Cauchy for trailing dimension one and a chi-square/Gaussian mixture for trailing dimension two, yielding the four CDFs. Arctangent inversion and strict endpoint asymptotics establish the exact two-dimensional contrast criterion and attained nontrivial minimum. A positive-sides squaring argument establishes the exact unique three-dimensional tolerance threshold. No numerical minimization or finite experiment is used as proof of the universal statements; `verify.py` reproduces consistency checks.

value.rationale: The two matrix–vector policies spend the same strictly defined operator-product budget. Their success comparison is not monotone in tolerance in two dimensions: fresh probes can outperform at both extremes while the deeper probe wins in between. Adding one trailing direction changes the phase topology to a single exact threshold. This is a motivated structural depth-versus-breadth stability boundary for randomized eigenvector approximation; it does not claim to optimize all two-query algorithms.
